item.title: Russia's war in Ukraine: the situation
item.description:
A US-brokered ceasefire in Oleshky has been extended across the Kherson region, with demining work creating a humanitarian corridor while similar local truces operate in other frontline cities. Russia is courting African leaders at a Moscow summit and President Putin is promoting Russia as a partner to the continent, while Trump officials discuss easing sanctions on a Russian investment fund. Russian drones have killed a Canadian volunteer rescuing animals in Donetsk and struck Moscow overnight, grounding flights at major airports. Investigators found Russia committed war crimes by targeting civilians, and 75,767 battle-related deaths in 2024 were recorded, according to UCDP.

item.title: Israel, Gaza and the West Bank: the situation
item.description:
Israeli forces have intensified a crackdown in Hebron, displacing thousands and prompting a UN warning of ethnic cleansing. The IDF has killed six Hamas operatives, including three who took part in the Oct. 7 attack, and three Hamas commanders in recent Gaza strikes. Israel’s parliamentary election remains deadlocked, with Netanyahu’s bloc leading but short of a majority and a record Arab turnout creating a dilemma for the opposition. The conflict produced 21,440 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Yemen and the Red Sea: the situation
item.description:
The Houthis have intensified attacks, striking Yemen's Aden airport and firing a ballistic missile toward Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery, while Saudi-led forces continue intercepting Houthi missiles aimed at the Eastern Province. Saudi airstrikes have hit a market in northern Yemen and a petrol station, causing civilian casualties. Egypt's parliament has approved military support to defend Saudi Arabia, linking the conflict to broader regional involvement. Russian satellites are now being used to guide Houthi strikes on Saudi targets, contributing to higher oil prices. The conflict caused 918 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Syria: the situation
item.description:
Jordan has resumed airstrikes in southern Syria against Daesh militants, prompting Syrian authorities to condemn the raids as a breach of airspace and to report civilian casualties. Syrian security forces killed a French jihadist in a shootout in Harem and another French fighter in Idlib, while unidentified gunmen killed two Syrian defence ministry personnel in Idlib. The two sides have reopened the Nasib border crossing and agreed to a joint security committee and investigation into the strikes. The conflict produced 2,732 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Iraq: the situation
item.description:
Iraqi courts sentenced seven French citizens, including six to life, for Islamic State membership, while security forces downed an unidentified drone over Baghdad. Baghdad and the Kurdistan Region deepened security coordination and weapons control, and Iraq announced it will host a 2028 OIC anti-corruption meeting. Prime Minister Al-Zaidi’s visit to Damascus advanced border security talks and oil links, and Turkey welcomed new Iraqi security steps in Sinjar. A sudden ouster of the Iraqi spy chief raised questions about the prime minister’s agenda, and Iraq’s development road plan promises 100,000 jobs. The conflict produced 396 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Sudan's civil war: the situation
item.description:
RSF drone strikes have intensified, hitting markets in Darfur, killing over 100 people, and targeting power stations such as Um Dabaker and another facility, cutting electricity to two states. The Sudanese army is accused of launching drone attacks from Ethiopian territory, while Ethiopia denies involvement, and Sudan repeatedly blames Ethiopia for attacks on civilian infrastructure. Women are increasingly serving as frontline responders as the siege worsens. The conflict has also spread nationwide, trapping civilians and prompting mass arrests. The war caused 4,680 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.description:

The SSPDF and SPLA-IO forces clashed in Wij-Panyikang, Upper Nile, and the UN commission warned that the peace deal is being dismantled. The UCDP recorded 2 battle-related deaths in 2024.

item.description:

AU peacekeepers are withdrawing from four bases in Lower Shabelle while the UN political mission in Somalia has ended without a replacement to address the election dispute. Algeria has deployed troops to Niger to protect energy assets, marking its first foreign mission in over 50 years, and Niger has accused Chad of a drone strike that killed two civilians. item.description:

Bandits also targeted APC supporters ahead of a rally in Katsina and abducted six residents from the Millennium City estate in Kaduna, while troops foiled a terrorist attack in Sokoto and rescued two abducted herders in Zamfara. Police in Benue arrested 34 suspected foreign nationals and rescued 29 kidnapping victims, and the Niger State Assembly praised the army for stopping a bandit raid. The conflict produced 1,486 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Iran and the regional confrontation: the situation
item.description:
Iran is pressing Qatar and the region to reopen the Strait of Hormuz while Houthi missiles and drones continue striking Saudi oil facilities and airports, prompting the reopening of Riyadh Airport after weeks of disruption. Qatar has urged Iran to show goodwill by ending threats and is reportedly ready to trade UN inspector access for sanctions relief, while Gulf states are working on a multipart peace deal to avert a renewal of the US-Iran war. War costs are estimated at $47 billion, according to the U.S. military.
